figures.alt: Thomas Holme's 1687 map of the improved part of Pennsylvania, showing surveyed parcels with owners' names along the Delaware River and a grid plan of Philadelphia in the inset
figures.caption: Holme's map of Pennsylvania (1687)

primary_sources: Thomas Holme, A Map of the Improved Part of the Province of Pennsylvania in America (1687)

options.misconception: The parcels were sold, not given — Penn's colony was a land business as well as a refuge.
options.text: Penn gave the land away for free to anyone who asked.
Penn surveyed the land and sold it in parcels to settlers.

options.misconception: The map is dedicated to Penn the proprietor, not the king — the parcels were sold to settlers.
options.text: The land was divided by the king among his courtiers in London.

options.misconception: The named parcels are English buyers — the map does not show Native ownership.
options.text: Native peoples owned and farmed most of the parcels shown.

rationales.A: The parcels carry owners' names because they were bought and sold — Penn's colony was a land business as well as a refuge.
rationales.B: Each parcel is surveyed and named for its buyer, and the map is dedicated to Penn, who held the charter and sold the land.
rationales.C: The map's dedication names Penn as proprietor; the parcels were sold to settlers, not granted by the king to courtiers.
rationales.D: The named parcels belong to English buyers; the map does not show Native ownership.
rationales.general:
1. Read the labels. Every parcel has a name — Radnor, Haverford, Germantown — a buyer, not a tribe.
2. Ask who drew the lines. A surveyor working for Penn, the proprietor who held the charter.
3. Ask what Penn was doing. Background: the king owed Penn's late father a large debt, and the charter paid it — Penn then repaid himself by selling land to settlers.
4. Name the pattern. Pennsylvania was a refuge and a real-estate business at the same time, and the map is the sales ledger drawn as a picture.
Remember: when a map names owners, it is showing you a market, not just a landscape.

stem: What does the map's grid of named parcels along the Delaware River best show about Pennsylvania?

stimulus.source_note: Map from the shared image pool; Thomas Holme, A Map of the Improved Part of the Province of Pennsylvania in America (1687), public domain.
stimulus.text: Thomas Holme's map of the improved part of Pennsylvania, surveyed for William Penn and published in 1687. The map shows the Delaware River along the bottom and the settled land divided into surveyed parcels, each marked with an owner's name — Radnor, Haverford, Germantown, and many others. In the upper right corner, an inset shows the city of Philadelphia laid out as a regular grid of streets. The Penn coat of arms fills the upper left corner, and the map is dedicated to William Penn, proprietor of Pennsylvania.
